testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a traffic violation suspends your regular driver's license, what happens to your CDL?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
A judge will decide if your CDL is suspended.

questions.explanation: A CDL is attached to your regular driver's license. Any suspension or revocation of your regular license, even for non-commercial driving, will also suspend or revoke your CDL.

questions.question: What two markings are usually on a front brake limiting valve?
questions.explanation: Some older air brake systems (made before 1975) have a front brake limiting valve with two settings: "normal" and "slippery."

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle must not lose more than 6 psi of air per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Which is allowed while driving a commercial vehicle?

options.text: You cannot text, but you can read texts.
You can text, but you cannot read texts.
You cannot text or read texts.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot text or read texts.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is illegal. This includes both writing and reading text messages.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check the engine oil level, coolant level, and condition of hoses.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when driving downhill?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls the vehicle downhill and causes speed to increase.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: Where are regrooved tires not allowed?

options.text: On the front wheels of a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front wheels of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver get in a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop at a safe distance and report the driver's behavior to police.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance and report the driver's behavior to police.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop safely away from the scene, wait for police, and tell them what you witnessed.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to drive a commercial vehicle across state lines?
questions.explanation: You must be at least 21 years old to drive a commercial vehicle between states. You can be 18 to drive one only within Michigan.

questions.question: A cargo van becomes:

options.text: The same height whether it has a heavy or light load.
Taller when it has a heavy load than when it has a light load.
Shorter when it has a heavy load than when it has a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorter when it has a heavy load than when it has a light load.
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower to the ground. A vehicle sits higher when it carries a light load and lower when it carries a heavy load. A vehicle that fits under an overpass when full may not fit when empty.

questions.question: While driving, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about what is happening on the sides of their vehicle.
Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Not worry about what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors regularly on both sides while driving and stay aware of the road ahead.

questions.question: In hot weather, tires should be checked regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
The tread wears down faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Heat causes air pressure in tires to increase. Check your tire pressure and condition carefully when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it swings during travel and has a high center of gravity.

questions.question: In the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain why you are checking each item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you are checking each item.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You will need to explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: If driving through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:
questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or moving water if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift into a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water, mud, and sand out of the brake mechanisms.

questions.question: Failing to drain air tanks could result in:

options.text: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
Too much air collecting in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: After two violations for hand-held mobile phone use:

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service.
You must drive 10 mph under the speed limit for a period of time.

questions.explanation: Two convictions for hand-held mobile phone use violations will result in CDL disqualification. Penalties increase with more violations.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Complete an after-trip inspection at the end of every trip, day, or shift. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and oil buildup. If these are not removed, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Front wheel braking will work:
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions. You are unlikely to experience a front wheel skid, even on ice.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only needed when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Before each trip, check for emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles, six fuses or three flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: Plan ahead with realistic travel times to reduce frustration. This helps prevent aggressive driving. Other ways to avoid aggressive driving include driving at safe speeds, keeping proper distance from other vehicles, and not making gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, you should:
questions.explanation: Manage your stress to reduce aggressive driving. If you realize you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. Drive at a safe speed.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, your best option is to:
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, look for a way to stop your vehicle. An escape ramp is the safest way to stop.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop soon after to check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop soon after to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: You may:

options.text: Have more than one license if one is for business.
Have more than one license if they are from different states.
Not have more than one license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not have more than one license.
questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver license at the same time. States share information to make sure no one has more than one license. Breaking this law can result in fines or jail time.

questions.question: When approaching a distracted driver, you should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space and keep a safe distance behind them.

questions.question: When braking on dry pavement at 55 mph, how much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: You are most likely to encounter strong winds when:
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to keep your vehicle in its lane. They are especially strong when you exit a tunnel.

questions.question: Using a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts the driver if the driver is speaking.

questions.explanation: A hands-free phone is safer than a hand-held phone, but it can still distract you. Talking on the phone takes your attention away from driving.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Make the change as soon as asked, without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: Check for traffic and use your turn signal before changing lanes. Always make sure it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Show other drivers that you are angry.
Warn other drivers that you are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are near.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers of your presence. Only use it when necessary, since it can startle other drivers.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, such as at dawn or dusk, a driver can be seen better by:

options.text: Flashing their lights on and off.

questions.explanation: Use your headlights on low beam at dawn, dusk, and in bad weather. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light stays on after starting the engine, it means:

options.text: The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS is not being used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light should turn off shortly after you start the engine. If it stays on, the ABS has a problem.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:

options.text: Differently each time to check different things.
The same way each time so you do not forget anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you do not forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you remember to check everything.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must be kept cold.
Children often run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are dangerous because children often run to them without checking for cars. They may not see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a driver should:

options.text: Watch for people getting out of the cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people getting out of the cars.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. A person may step out without looking, or a parked car may start moving. Watch for these dangers.

questions.question: Driving a refrigerated truck carrying hanging meat:

options.text: Is a good way for new drivers to gain experience.

questions.explanation: A skilled driver is needed to transport hanging meat. The load is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the meat swings, which affects how the truck handles.

questions.question: Except during the straight line backing test, a driver may exit their vehicle to check its position up to:
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during a test. You can do this a maximum of two times during most exercises. During the straight line backing exercise, you can only do it once.

questions.question: What is usually found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage brakes if they build up in the system. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Acceptable if you are eating foods that are easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes your attention away from the road and is dangerous. Plan ahead and stop to eat during long trips.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, a lack of spray from other vehicles' tires means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is caught under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, no spray from other tires means ice has formed. Be extra careful when driving on wet roads in freezing weather.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you should inspect it:

options.text: Only at the beginning of a drive.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.explanation: Check your cargo and its straps before you start driving. During the trip, check within the first 50 miles, every 3 hours or 150 miles, and after each break.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, you should:

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal followed by the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to light up your brake lights.
Swerve from side to side to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to light up your brake lights.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights and alert drivers behind you that you are slowing down. Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: For a basic vehicle control skills test, you should be able to:

options.text: Weave between a line of cones.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes straight line backing, offset backing (right and left), driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of a tired driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of tired driving include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, disconnected thinking, not remembering miles driven, missing exits, trouble keeping your head up, drifting lanes, following too closely, hitting shoulder rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, the rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. This happens when the driver:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes the rods out and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: The center of gravity in a trailer should be:

options.text: At the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Keep the weight of cargo as low as possible in your vehicle. A center of gravity that is too high increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: If you are unfamiliar with an area where you must back up, you should:

options.text: Get out of your vehicle and walk around the area to learn about it.
Not use both side mirrors because it can be distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up in the area so you can see how they do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of your vehicle and walk around the area to learn about it.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of your vehicle and look at where you will go. Check for obstacles on the sides and overhead.
